full_judgment: 7. Defendant Nos. 1 to 3 felt aggrieved of the above adjudication and sought setting aside same through a medium of appeal being Other Appeal No. 83 of 1991 in the Court of District Judge Rangpur, Learned Sub-Judge and Artha Rin Adalat No. 1 Rangpur heard the appeal and by Judgment and decree dated 29-11-1992 allowed it, set aside Judgment and decree recorded in Other Suit No. 104 of 1990 and dismissed the suit. In recording dismissal, learned appellate Judge being the last and final Judge of fact considered evidences both oral and documentary and other materials on record. Learned appellate Judge taking into account Exhibit-Kha and Kha-1, Cadestral Survey Khatian Ras. 69 and 94 found that property of those two Cadastral Survey Khatians stood recorded in the names of Sreeman, son of Ram Singh, Rajani, son of Lili, in four annas equ-al share. Learned appellate Judge taking into consideration of Exhibit- Kha and Kha(1) also found that name of the father of Sreeman Barman was Ram Singh. Learned appellate Judge on consideration of testimonies of DWs 3, 5 and 6 and also testimony of PW 2 found that all of them substantially supported the case of defendants that Sreeman, LiIi, Dip and Rai Chand were full brothers and son of Ram Singh. Learned Appellate Judge found that PW 1 himself admitted that entry in Cadestral Survey Khatian Nos. 69 and 94, Exhibit-Kha and Kha(l) were true entries. Learned Appellate Judge also found that there was no explanation from the plaintiff side as to why the land of Cadestral Survey Khatian Nos. 69 and 94 had been recorded in four ann as equal share in the name of Sreeman and successor of Lili, Rai Chand and Dip Chand. Learned Appellate Judge on assessment on the testimony of PW 2 and DWs3 and 6 positively found that at the time of alleged pattan in 1346 BS Plaintiff Kailash was a mere infant of 8/9 years of age. Learned appellate Judge also on a careful scrutiny of Rent Receipts Exhibits- 3 to 3(Ga) found that Rent Receipts had not been written and signed by Kailash Chandra who was a boy of 8/9 years of age and a student of class-IV Learned appellate Judge also noted that hand writing and signature appeared to be of the product of matured hand. Learned appellate Judge also found that Rent Receipts had been purposely created subsequently collecting those. Learned appellate Judge discarded the claim of plaintiffs that Kailash granted settlement of his share of lot Nos. 1,2 and 3. Learned appellate Judge also found that Revisional Settlement Record of Right published in the name of plaintiff No.1 in sixteen annas share was wrong and without foundation. Learned appellate Judge on assessment of the testimonies of witnesses of both the parties found that testimonies of defendant's witnesses were more reliable and trustworthy than the testimonies of the witnesses for the plaintiffs. Learned appellate Judge, thereafter, found that exclusive possession of plaintiffs over the suit property had not been proved. Learned appellate Judge recorded positive decision that defendant had been able to establish their co-sharership in the suit jotes and the claim of plaintiffs exclusive possession over the suit property did not arise. Further positive decision rendered by learned Judge is that defendants got joint possession over suit property.
